title: Ward 10 vacancy filled and committee appointments
subtitle: Firefighters' agreement, Stirling Avenue shelter agreement, AMPS hearing officers, and committee chairs and board appointments.
overview: Council chose to fill the vacant Ward 10 seat by appointing a 2022 election candidate, Stephanie Stretch, rather than holding a by-election {{vote:m2}}. The City Clerk will confirm qualifications and consent, and an appointment by-law will come to the next Council meeting.

Council also approved a new collective agreement for 2023-2026 with the Kitchener Professional Firefighters' Association {{vote:m5}}. It authorized the CAO to sign a non-binding agreement with the Region of Waterloo setting out responsibilities for the emergency homeless shelter at 104 Stirling Avenue South {{vote:m4}}. Five hearing officers were appointed for the City's parking and non-parking administrative penalty system through December 2026 {{vote:m1}}.

Council named chairs and vice-chairs for its three standing committees and filled seats on local boards and advisory committees. Ward 10 seats on the Downtown BIA and the Downtown Action and Advisory Committee were held back until the new member is appointed. The Kitchener in Bloom appointment was set aside while staff review the program.

decisions.detail: Council selected appointment of a 2022 election candidate, Stephanie Stretch, to fill the Ward 10 vacancy, with the by-law to follow at the next meeting.
Council approved the Memorandum of Settlement establishing the 2023-2026 collective agreement with the Kitchener Professional Firefighters' Association.
The CAO was authorized to sign a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Region of Waterloo on accountabilities for the emergency shelter.
Five hearing officers were appointed through December 2026, with existing honoraria of $260 per half day and $520 per full day approved and indemnification confirmed.

debate: Discussion of the Ward 10 vacancy was brief, since the revised motion had already been dealt with at committee, and no one asked for the two committee items to be voted on separately.

Councillors asked who sets the Ward 10 seats on the Downtown BIA and the Downtown Action and Advisory Committee. Staff said Council-approved terms of reference specify them, so Council can change them.

On Kitchener in Bloom, one councillor worried the recognition program could fade. Staff said a proposal to re-energize it without the current advisory committee had been in the works and asked for time to consult staff. The item was pulled to come back later.
For the Climate Change and Environmental Committee, councillors noted that only one member of Council had sat on it before, and left the seat open in case the new Ward 10 member is interested.
Before the firefighters' agreement vote, one councillor thanked staff and noted the value of several successive freely negotiated agreements.
